title: A seal records the result and not the scope, so its reach cannot be derived later
body:
# 0034: A seal records the result and not the scope, so its reach cannot be derived later

## Tags

gates, seals, provenance, reach, highlander, false-green, D19

## Summary

A seal log states its VERDICT and says nothing about what that verdict covers. Three of Lamplight's four gate legs -- `rust`, `credo`, `mix` -- write no provenance line at all. Only `lua` does, hand-rolled inside the leg itself.

**A seal's verdict does not rot; the sentence about its REACH does.** Reach is the answer to "what tree was this measured against, and what has landed since" -- and today it can only be reconstructed by hand, by a reader who already knows the run window. Nothing in the seal states the window, so the reconstruction starts from a guess.

The `lua` leg already carries the whole argument in a comment block written when the defect was found there:

> a reader a day later could see the RESULT and never the SCOPE. That is invisible for a gate whose lane is fixed, and load-bearing for this one, because this lane can be legitimately narrowed. `--only framework` runs 49 of 307 cases and passes them all -- an honest, complete run of exactly what was requested [...] Its SEAL said `49 test(s), 49 passed` and nothing else, and the only way to tell that from a degraded run was to already know the lane is 307.

That reasoning is correct and it is not lua-specific. It was applied to one leg and left off the other three.

## Reproduction

Lamplight, seal set `20260825-1020` (RUST) / `20260825-1021` (CREDO, LUA, MIX). Positive control included, so the absence is measured rather than assumed:

    $ for L in RUST CREDO LUA MIX; do
        f=$(ls tmp/test/20260825-10*.$L.out | head -1)
        printf "%-6s %s SCOPE line(s)\n" "$L" "$(grep -c '^SCOPE:' "$f")"
      done
    RUST   0 SCOPE line(s)
    CREDO  0 SCOPE line(s)
    LUA    1 SCOPE line(s)
    MIX    0 SCOPE line(s)

The one that exists is line 1 of the LUA log:

    SCOPE: bin/lamplight test lua (none -- every declared default root)

## What it cost, today

Answering "does the current seal reach the tree?" required deriving the window from the FILENAME, then running the reach query by hand:

    $ git log --since='2026-08-25 10:21' --oneline -- 'apps/**' 'native/**'
    798fccba8 fix(wrighter,cli): two Wrighters shared one discovery slot, and the loser went unreachable
    133133c75 fix(cli): doctor closed with a verdict on planes it never reached
    07794cb08 fix(ic): a live invite token in the log stream, and the premise that put it there

Three commits above the green, the first of them 16 files and ~1,350 insertions across `apps/control`, `apps/wrighter` and `native/cli`. **None of that is visible from the seal, and a reader who did not think to ask would have read four green legs as covering the tree.**

Two things made the hand-derivation worse than it needed to be. The filename stamp is LOCAL, so it is not directly comparable to anything stamped UTC. And the legs do not share a stamp -- RUST is `1020` where the other three are `1021` -- so "the run window" is not a single value the seal set agrees on.

## The second failure mode: provenance found by content grep is a false positive

A reader looking for provenance by grepping the log gets hits that are not provenance. In the same MIX seal:

    $ grep -c 'measured:' tmp/test/20260825-1021.MIX.out
    2
    $ grep -c '^measured:' tmp/test/20260825-1021.MIX.out
    0

Both hits are ExUnit TEST NAMES -- two ST0344 cases whose titles contain the word. A provenance line must therefore be findable by POSITION and a distinctive key, never by searching the log's body for a word. The corpus a gate runs over is arbitrary text and will eventually contain any key chosen.


## Confirmed on a live full run, 2026-08-25

Lamplight ran its four gates green at `20260825-1751` (RUST) / `-1752` (CREDO, LUA, MIX). **The runner printed the provenance and no seal file kept it:**

    verdict: /Users/matts/.../tmp/test/20260825-1752.MIX.errors
    measured: d7218e6c8
    overhead: 1.01x -- 887s wall against 876.94s of reported test time across 10 suite(s).

    $ for f in tmp/test/20260825-17*.{out,errors}; do grep -c '^measured:' "$f"; done
    0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0

**All eight files, both kinds, zero.** So `measured:` is real, correct, and reaches only the terminal of whoever ran the gate -- which is the precise shape of R4. The sha was independently recorded before the run by a reader who wanted the reach answerable afterwards, and it matched; **that hand-written note is the artifact this issue asks the runner to produce.** Without it the reach question would have started from the local filename stamp, which the four legs do not share.

Note also what the run DOES print and keep: `overhead: 1.01x` and per-suite counts land in the seal. **The numbers that describe the run's cost survive; the one that identifies what it measured does not.**

## Third instance, 2026-08-26 -- and two of its own predicates expired under re-measurement

Seal set `20260826-0128` (RUST) / `-0129` (CREDO, LUA, MIX). Measured by Lamplight's vc, re-derived independently here on hv's ruling that the node recording a result should not also be the instrument that produced it. **Re-running rather than relaying the numbers is what produced everything below the first table.**

**Positive control first, per the rule this issue already states.** LUA line 1, count 1: `SCOPE: bin/lamplight test lua (none -- every declared default root)`. It reproduces verbatim, so the zeros below are a measurement rather than a broken grep.

| file                         | bytes   | `^measured:` | `^SCOPE:` |
| ---------------------------- | ------- | ------------ | --------- |
| `20260826-0128.RUST.out`     | 21526   | 0            | 0         |
| `20260826-0128.RUST.errors`  | 0       | 0            | --        |
| `20260826-0129.CREDO.out`    | 320     | 0            | 0         |
| `20260826-0129.CREDO.errors` | 0       | 0            | --        |
| `20260826-0129.LUA.out`      | 56081   | 0            | **1**     |
| `20260826-0129.LUA.errors`   | 0       | 0            | --        |
| `20260826-0129.MIX.out`      | 2870524 | 0            | 0         |
| `20260826-0129.MIX.errors`   | 0       | 0            | --        |

**Read the bytes column before the count column.** Four of the eight files are ZERO BYTES, and `grep -c` returns 0 on an empty file for any pattern whatever. So "zero across all eight, both kinds" is four measurements and four vacuous rows: the informative denominator is 4, not 8. The verdict is unchanged; the predicate is now stated honestly beside it, which is what this issue asks of everybody else.

The `measured` false-positive documented above also reproduces on a second corpus. Unanchored, `grep -c 'measured'` hits 21 lines in RUST.out and 22 in MIX.out -- every RUST hit is cargo's own `0 measured;` benchmark field, every MIX hit is an ExUnit test NAME. Anchoring to `^measured:` is what makes the zero real. R6, live, on a corpus nobody chose for it.

### The reach query has gone from a false green to a false precision

vc measured the query this issue documents as EMPTY -- `git log --since='2026-08-26 01:28' --oneline -- 'apps/**' 'native/**'`, no output, rc=0, which reads as NOTHING LANDED. Re-run roughly six hours later it is not empty:

    e7c590f53  2026-08-26 11:32  fix(ic): a typed error naming the wrong cause, and four pointers to things that moved
    81d17e178  2026-08-26 11:28  fix(cli): content-proven is built -- the source-path proxy no longer downgrades the engine verdict

**Neither commit touches `mix.lock`**, and ten dependency rows moved uncommitted at 10:25. So the same predicate, over the same run, gave two different answers six hours apart, and NEITHER of them mentions the change that actually moved the build's inputs. **An empty answer at least invites suspicion. Two named commits read as a complete account of what landed, so the failure got worse over those six hours rather than better.**

### The dependency movement, re-derived

Ten rows in `mix.lock`, uncommitted, and they are real version moves rather than checksum churn (sampled 3 of 10):

    arca_cli            git ffc43f3069f2 -> 12fe2cf94247
    ash_authentication  4.14.1 -> 4.14.2
    phoenix             1.8.12 -> 1.8.13

Sampling 4 of the 10 for timing (`arca_cli`, `ash_authentication`, `phoenix`, `oban`), all four agree: `deps/` fetched **10:25 BST**, `_build/test/lib/` compiled **10:29 BST**, `mix.lock` touched **10:25 BST** -- against a run window of **01:29 to 01:45 BST**. Every one of those is strictly AFTER the run, so the run necessarily linked the pre-bump set.

### One of the three predicates did NOT reproduce, and that is the finding

vc recorded `_build/test/lib/ash_authentication` as compiled `2026-08-24 08:47` and not since. It now reads **`2026-08-26 10:29 BST`**. `_build` is mutable and it moved between one node measuring it and another re-measuring it the same day. **The conclusion survives on a stabler predicate** -- fetch and compile both strictly after the run window, which any further recompile only reinforces -- **but the original predicate is retired rather than repeated**, because an argument resting on "this mtime is old" expires the moment anything touches the file.

That is two of the three evidence items behind this instance changing under re-measurement within a day, and neither change was announced by anything. **The reach question is asked LATER by definition, and every artefact available to answer it here is mutable filesystem state.** That is the case for R9, and it is why R9 asks for a value to compare rather than a state to inspect.

### What could not be established, and it is R3 live

Whether the overnight run was `test all` or four separately narrowed invocations **cannot be determined from the seal set at all**. The only provenance that survived is the LUA leg's own line 1, which records THAT LEG's invocation and is silent on the parent that called it. hv called this run 100% green; the seal cannot say what it was green over.

## Requirements

Numbered so they can be cited individually.

- **R1.** Every gate that writes a seal writes a provenance header -- not only the gate whose lane can narrow. A fixed-lane gate still needs its tree and window recorded.
- **R2.** The header is written BEFORE the stream, and the stream APPENDS. The lua leg's reasoning holds and should be preserved: `tee` truncates, and a header written into the pipe instead puts the brace group's status into `PIPESTATUS`, silently replacing the task's own exit code with the `printf`'s.
- **R3.** It states what was ASKED FOR -- the full invocation including arguments -- and says so explicitly when there were none (`(none -- every declared default root)`), rather than rendering blank. A blank field and an unnarrowed run must not look alike.
- **R4.** It states the TREE the run was measured against: HEAD sha, plus whether the working tree was dirty at start. Without this, reach cannot be derived at all -- only guessed at from the filename.
- **R5.** It states a UTC start stamp read from a clock. The filename stamp is local, the legs do not share it, and its relationship to the run window is stated nowhere.
- **R6.** Fixed position (line 1) and a distinctive key, so the header is found by position and never by grepping the body. See the `measured:` false positive above.
- **R7.** A no-op when there is no log. The `--no-out` case CI uses must not fail or warn because provenance had nowhere to go.
- **R8.** ONE primitive in `lib/runlog`, called by every leg. Not per-leg copies. The single existing copy inside Lamplight's `cmd/test.d/lua` is the fork to retire in the same change.
- **R9.** The header states a DIGEST of the build's DECLARED INPUTS -- `sha256(mix.lock)`, `sha256(Cargo.lock)` and their per-language equivalents -- so a later reader COMPARES a value instead of reconstructing from mtimes. **R4 is necessary and not sufficient: it is incomplete rather than wrong, and it stays.** R4 records the tree at run START, and the reach question is asked later. On 2026-08-26 the tree WAS clean at start, so R4's dirty flag would have reported clean, correctly, and still misled -- ten dependency rows moved uncommitted nine hours afterwards, invisible to a HEAD-sha comparison and invisible to a dirty flag read at the start. Of the three artefacts a later reader might use, the digest is the only one that cannot rot.

## Notes on placement

Filed here rather than fixed in the consumer deliberately. Lamplight's `bin/.devbin/` is vendored and tracked (98 files); a per-leg fix there is four edits the next re-vendor clobbers, and it would fork a primitive that every project in both fleets needs. `bin/lamplight` is devbin's own launcher, so it is not a consumer-side seam either. Lamplight is the requirements provider; the capability belongs in `lib/runlog`.

R8 is what makes this a devbin issue rather than a Lamplight one. Everything above R8 could be satisfied four times over in a consumer, and that is precisely the outcome to avoid.



## Closed 2026-09-16 on hv's ruling -- met by later fixes, with R4 and R9 delegated to the project by design

Assessed by vc against the tree at `444598d`, requirement by requirement, and measured on one live `bin/devbin check all` in devbin's own tree (run `fde7be9f`, stamp `20260916-1606`) rather than read from comments alone.

- **R1, R2, R6, R8 -- met.** `run_gate` in `lib/runlog` calls `note_invocation` for every gate, BEFORE the tool runs, and the stream then appends (`tee -a`). It is one primitive, and every line carries the fixed `devbin| ` prefix at the top of the log. All five `.out` files of the live run opened with it.
- **R3 -- met in substance.** The header records the platform, the run id (issue 0045), where the command line came from (`from: config key commands.check.options.critic.run`), and the full argv, one argument per line, so it is never blank. Whether a set of seals was one `check all` or several narrowed invocations is now answered by the shared run id, which is the question R3's third instance could not answer.
- **R5 -- the two faults it named are fixed, although the stamp is not written into the header.** The filename stamp is UTC (`date -u`) and is set once per invocation and exported (`bin/devbin`, `DEVBIN_RUN_STAMP`), so the legs of one run share it. Measured: all five legs of the live run are `20260916-1606`, where this issue's instances had RUST at `1020` and the others at `1021`, in local time.
- **R4 and R9 -- delegated, deliberately.** `measured:` now reaches the kept artefact before the seal (issue 0046, `note_referent`), and its value is whatever the project's `project.referent` command answers. devbin is forbidden to parse that string (`lib/runlog`, `_referent_line`), so a HEAD sha, a dirty flag and a lockfile digest are composed by the project, which is where the knowledge of which lockfiles matter lives. hv ruled on 2026-09-16 that this delegation is the answer to R4 and R9.
- **R7 -- not re-measured for this closure.**
